classification.difficultyReason: Translate the shared 29-hour threshold into different quartile proportions and battery counts, then identify maximum observed life as a criterion favouring Grade B despite its lower median. The earlier parts scaffold the boxplot comparison.

content.prompt: The ‘life’ of alkaline batteries is compared through continuous use in a standard product. 40 Grade A and 40 Grade B batteries are tested in this way. Their results are shown in the two boxplots below.

spec.description: Grade B above Grade A on one horizontal axis with unit ticks and labels at 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35. Unfilled boxes; whiskers have no terminal caps. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Grade B five-number summary: 24, 25, 26, 29, 32 hours. Grade A five-number summary: 27, 28, 29, 30, 31 hours.
spec.answerVisibility: All plotted summaries are permanent student-visible givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the median battery life for the Grade A and Grade B batteries.

answer.short: Grade A: 29 hours; Grade B: 26 hours.
answer.worked: Read the line inside each box: Grade A has median 29 hours and Grade B has median 26 hours.

children.label: b
children.prompt: State the range in battery life for the Grade A and Grade B batteries.

answer.short: Grade A: 4 hours; Grade B: 8 hours.
answer.worked:
Range is maximum minus minimum.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Grade A range}&=31-27=4\text{ hours}\\\text{Grade B range}&=32-24=8\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: State the interquartile range for the Grade A and Grade B batteries.

answer.short: Grade A: 2 hours; Grade B: 4 hours.
answer.worked:
Read the box edges as the lower and upper quartiles. The interquartile range is $Q_3-Q_1$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Grade A IQR}&=30-28=2\text{ hours}\\\text{Grade B IQR}&=29-25=4\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Determine the number of Grade A and Grade B batteries lasting longer than 29 hours.

answer.short: Grade A: 20 batteries; Grade B: 10 batteries.
answer.worked:
For Grade A, 29 hours is the median, so 50% last longer. For Grade B, 29 hours is the upper quartile, so 25% last longer.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Grade A count}&=0.50\times40=20\\\text{Grade B count}&=0.25\times40=10\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Describe the shape of data distributions for the Grade A and Grade B battery life.

answer.short: Grade A: symmetrical; Grade B: positively skewed.
answer.worked: Grade A is symmetrical: its median is central in the box and its whiskers have equal lengths. Grade B is positively skewed: the spread above its median is greater, with a longer right whisker.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Under what criterion is the Grade B battery ‘better’ than the Grade A battery in this test?

answer.short: Maximum battery life: a Grade B battery lasted 32 hours, longer than any Grade A battery.
answer.worked: Compare the right whisker endpoints. Grade B has a maximum life of 32 hours, compared with 31 hours for Grade A. Grade B is better if the criterion is the longest individual battery life observed in these samples.
